candidate: Controller-owned research loop: harness code owns commit, verify, keep or revert and state; the agent only proposes and edits (pattern from Hard to Fool arXiv 2611.06607 v1, codex-autoresearch v0.6.0, RankEvolve arXiv 2609.39551 v1)
what: A loop command in the run controller that executes each iteration as a fixed sequence (propose, edit inside an allowlist, launch, measure with the frozen evaluator, decide by fixed gates, commit or revert, record) and calls the agent only for the propose and edit steps.
problem_here: Goal 1 requires that harness code and a frozen evaluator decide what is kept. The popular loop skills leave the keep decision to the agent, and agents given a protocol as text skip gates and stop early.
mechanism: Stdlib state machine. Acceptance is a conjunction of absolute gates fixed before the run: gain over the incumbent larger than the measured noise floor, guard metrics within floors, finite metrics, sample floors. Out-of-scope edits, HEAD drift, malformed metrics and timeouts stop the loop. Budget exhaustion is recorded as a pause, never as success.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/html/2611.06607v1 (2026-11-04, single author: 28 campaigns, headline candidate rejected at holdout, Sharpe 2.94 discovery against 0.26 holdout); https://github.com/leo-lilinxiao/codex-autoresearch (v0.6.0, 2026-06-02: control script owns commits, verification, rollback and state); https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.39551 (2026-09-30, authors: in 10 pilot runs with a prompt-only protocol 4 stopped early, 4 skipped a gate, all 10 ran a subset of proposals); https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00384 (2026-10-30, LinkedIn: external orchestrator owns trials, history, selection and budgets). All self-reported; no controlled comparison of controller-owned against agent-owned keep decisions was found.
maturity: Pattern, no dependency. Sources read: codex-autoresearch v0.5.0 (2026-05-13) and v0.6.0 (2026-06-02), MIT, about 3.2k stars (weak signal); Hard to Fool v1 (2026-11-04, CC BY 4.0, one author).
cost: Medium: a state machine, gates and tests in the controller; must work without POSIX process groups on native Windows; a too-strict gate set can reject every change; the agent can still cheat inside the training code it edits, so this needs evaluator locking beside it.
simpler_alternative: Prose procedure in the skill with the agent applying keep or discard (what most loop skills do).
reason: It is the stated goal, every cheating statistic in this sweep argues for it, and it needs only the standard library.
cheap_local_trial: On a 2-minute toy training script, script a fake agent that submits five edits (one out of scope, one that changes the evaluator, one real gain, one within noise, one that prints a fake metric line) and check the controller keeps only the real gain.

candidate: Three-tier data with a once-only holdout opened behind an irreversible receipt (Hard to Fool arXiv 2611.06607 v1; Hidden Consistent Evaluation, AIRA_2 arXiv 2603.26499 v2)
what: Search split for keep decisions, a confirmation split used a limited number of times to pick the final candidate, and the sealed test set opened once by the final-evaluation command after a receipt is durably written.
problem_here: Fifty keep-or-revert decisions against one validation set bias the kept score; the kit seals the test set today but has no record that makes a second look impossible after a crash or a rerun.
mechanism: Before unsealing, the controller appends a receipt event (candidate commit, evaluator hash, time) to the ledger and syncs it to disk; the final-evaluation command refuses to run if a receipt already exists; a crash after the receipt still counts as the one use; the loop worker stops at a ready-for-holdout state and cannot open the holdout itself.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/html/2611.06607v1 (2026-11-04, author-measured: validation Sharpe 3.34 against holdout 0.26 for the headline candidate); https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.40303 (2026-09-30, EPFL and Apple: self-selected results trail the oracle choice by 1.9 to 6.8 points); https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.05398 (2026-10-04, authors: final submissions trail the best evaluated candidate by up to 5.38 points); https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.26499 (2026-04-13, Meta: names the validation-selection gap as a bottleneck). Protocol details of Hidden Consistent Evaluation come from a search summary only (Unverified).
maturity: Method, no dependency. Holdout-receipt design read in a paper of 2026-11-04 by one author; the selection-gap evidence comes from three 2026 papers (EPFL and Apple; Meta; the MMPostTrainBench authors).
cost: Low code cost; costs data (a third split) and can leave a user with a consumed holdout after a crash, which is the point but will surprise; the receipt must survive on Windows file systems (flush and atomic rename).
simpler_alternative: Keep the current sealed test set with the unseal token and trust the journal.
reason: Validity is the top-ranked attribute and this closes the one gap the current seal leaves open, with standard-library code.
cheap_local_trial: Run the final-evaluation command twice on a toy repository and kill it once mid-run; confirm the second and third attempts are refused and the ledger shows one receipt.

candidate: Hash-chained append-only run ledger with trial counting and duplicate refusal (Hard to Fool arXiv 2611.06607 v1; events log in codex-autoresearch v0.6.0)
what: A JSON-lines ledger in which every event stores the SHA-256 of the previous event; the controller counts trials against the budget and refuses a proposal whose normalized content matches an earlier one before any GPU time is spent.
problem_here: A reviewer must be able to verify each kept result from saved artifacts, and failed or reverted runs must stay on record; the current journal is a Markdown file the agent edits.
mechanism: hashlib chain plus a verify command that fails closed on edit, removal or reorder; invalid proposals are logged without spending a trial; duplicate detection on a hash of the diff and the launch arguments; optional cap on proposals per idea family.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/html/2611.06607v1 (2026-11-04, single author, design described and used for 28 campaigns); https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.30541 (2026-09-24, ICDM 2026 applied track: one setting re-tested at least 6 times and a prohibited operation repeated 6 times despite written instructions); https://github.com/leo-lilinxiao/codex-autoresearch (v0.6.0: append-only events file, contradictory state is an error). No measurement of the ledger itself exists.
maturity: Technique, no dependency; hash chaining is decades old; the loop-specific use is from 2026.
cost: Low: about 150 lines and tests. A chain stored beside the agent can be rewritten wholesale, so the guard must deny agent writes to it and the head hash should be echoed somewhere the agent cannot edit; near-duplicate proposals with trivial differences slip past an exact hash.
simpler_alternative: Plain append-only JSON-lines file protected by the existing guard, without chaining.
reason: Cheap, offline, and it turns three recurring failures (omitted negatives, repeated experiments, edited history) into checks.
cheap_local_trial: Write 20 events, edit one line by hand, and confirm the verify command names the first broken link; submit the same diff twice and confirm the second is refused without a launch.

candidate: Fresh agent session per iteration with all loop state in files (the flush half of Fork-and-Flush arXiv 2610.07447 v1; background mode of codex-autoresearch v0.6.0)
what: Each iteration starts a new headless agent session that receives a short generated brief (incumbent, budget left, a capped digest of what was tried) instead of continuing one long conversation.
problem_here: Long sessions anchor on past attempts, shrink their edits and lose state at compaction; an unattended overnight loop is exactly the long session where this happens.
mechanism: The controller launches the agent once per iteration with a brief built from the ledger; nothing but files carries over; the digest is size-capped so history cannot crowd out the task.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.07447 (2026-10-05, authors: flush-only 0.55 against 0.45 for a single run on 11 tasks, 5 runs each, no confidence intervals); https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20563 (2026-10-14, authors: plateau as history accumulates); https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.40303 (2026-09-30: 9.5 compactions per 24-hour run at a 64k limit, each discarding about 76% of context); https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21082 (authors: models at medium effort were less accurate with the project record than without). Counter-evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05108 (2026-11-03: persistent agents were more efficient, though not better on final held-out results).
maturity: Pattern; shipped in codex-autoresearch v0.6.0 (2026-06-02, one headless worker per iteration) and practised in two practitioner write-ups; no independent replication of the measured gain.
cost: Each fresh session pays start-up tokens to re-read the brief; requires a headless mode on all three agent products; a poor digest repeats old ideas, so it depends on duplicate refusal.
simpler_alternative: One long session with the existing post-compaction status hook.
reason: Near-free in a controller-owned loop, removes the compaction problem, and the measured direction is positive in every source read.
cheap_local_trial: Run 10 iterations of the 5-minute autoresearch task twice, once as one session and once with a new session per iteration, and compare best score, distinct ideas tried and tokens.

candidate: Fork-and-Flush scheduled branching (arXiv 2610.07447 v1; productised in uditgoenka/autoresearch v2.3.0)
what: At fixed points of the budget the loop starts several branches from the incumbent, each with fresh context, and continues from the best one.
problem_here: A loop that stalls in one family of ideas wastes the rest of its budget.
mechanism: K=4 branches at 33% and 66% of the budget, each given about 6% of the budget, files inherited, chat history dropped, best branch by score continues.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.07447 (2026-10-05, authors: normalized score 0.47 single run, 0.54 best-of-4, 0.78 fork-and-flush on 13 tasks; ablation 0.45, 0.55 flush only, 0.57 fork only, 0.71 both; a plateau trigger rarely fired). Branches are selected on the same score that is reported, one model family, one harness, no confidence intervals, no independent replication found on 2026-11-11.
maturity: Paper v1 2026-10-05 (CC BY 4.0, no code); third-party implementation released 2026-10-31 (MIT, about 6.8k stars, weak signal).
cost: About half the budget goes to branch rounds; on one GPU branches run in sequence; branch selection needs a split other than the reported one or it adds selection bias; more state to recover after preemption.
simpler_alternative: Fresh session per iteration without branching.
reason: Largest measured loop-design effect in the sweep, but unreplicated and measured on code-optimization tasks with cheap evaluations, not on training runs.
cheap_local_trial: On the 5-minute autoresearch task with a 6-hour budget, compare one run of plain fresh-session looping with one run that forks 3 branches at one third and two thirds; repeat twice; select branches on a confirmation split.

candidate: Forgetting: periodic reset of sessions and candidate history with restart from the best candidate (arXiv 2610.20563 v1)
what: At intervals the loop discards the agent-visible history of attempts and continues from the incumbent only.
problem_here: Accumulated history makes agents repeat themselves and make smaller edits.
mechanism: A restart rule in the controller: after N iterations or on a stagnation signal, the next brief contains the incumbent and the task only; the ledger stays complete for the harness and the reviewer.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20563 (2026-10-14, abstract, authors: up to 15% over parallel agents and up to 39% over a single agent on four tasks including model training). Details (three runs per configuration, 20 dollars per replicate, edit size falling from about 150 to 30 lines) come from a secondary overview at https://www.alphaxiv.org/overview/2610.20563 and are Inferred. The paper clears sessions and history together and leaves when to forget open.
maturity: Paper v1 2026-10-14, CC BY 4.0, no code, no replication found.
cost: Small in code; risks re-trying known failures unless duplicate refusal stays active while the agent cannot see why a proposal was refused.
simpler_alternative: A size-capped digest of past attempts in every brief.
reason: Cheap to implement as an option of the fresh-session loop; evidence is one author-run study whose full text could not be read.
cheap_local_trial: Same task and budget as the Fork-and-Flush trial, comparing a capped digest in every brief against an empty digest every 8 iterations.

candidate: Minimal-harness rules: pull-style budget and hardware query, no injected nudges, short default prompt, no delegation by default (How Much of a Harness, arXiv 2609.40303 v1)
kind: design rule and small core feature
what: A read-only controller command that reports time, runs, GPU-hours and tokens left plus GPU utilisation, called by the agent when it wants it; no periodic reminders; default instructions kept short with depth loaded on demand.
problem_here: An unattended agent must respect limits without anyone prompting it, and the kit's premise that elaborate scaffolds do not help needs current evidence.
mechanism: A budget subcommand prints one compact line; the controller enforces the limits itself; the skill tells the agent the command exists and nothing else pushes time information into context.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.40303 and https://machinelearning.apple.com/research/harness-autonomous-ml-engineering (2026-09-30, EPFL and Apple, MLE-bench 30 tasks, 24 hours, one GPU): removing the system and jobs tools cost 8.9 medal points (CI 1.7 to 15.9); time nudges lowered medal rate from 59.4% to 48.9%; delegation 55.7% to 45.2%; broadcast with parallelism 33.3%; a minimal prompt raised a weaker model from 20.3% to 23.9%; strict validation guidance narrowed the self-select gap from 5.433 to 3.833. Corroboration: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.39551 (current-step-only instructions beat full-protocol injection by 2.1 to 10.4 points); https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.18088 (skills and orchestration did not reliably help); https://benchmarks.bespokelabs.ai/autoresearchexam/ (agents are shown remaining time).
maturity: Controlled ablations in one paper by authors from EPFL and Apple, v1 2026-09-30, no code; open-weight models and one agent product only.
cost: Very low; the risk is over-generalising from one benchmark family and from weaker models than the three target products use.
simpler_alternative: Keep the current skill text and add a time-remaining line to the status hook (a nudge, which the evidence says to avoid).
reason: Strongest controlled evidence in the sweep, consistent with the brief, and it removes features instead of adding them.
cheap_local_trial: Add the budget command, run two short loops on a toy task with a 30-minute cap, one with a reminder injected every iteration and one with the query command only, and compare overrun, final score and tokens.

candidate: Evaluator locking combined with data-access control, patch tracking and file-access logging (RewardHackingAgents arXiv 2603.11337 v1)
what: The evaluator and metric code are hashed and compared before every scoring step, scoring runs from a pristine copy outside the agent's writable scope, held-out data is unreadable by training code, and each run records which files changed and which were read.
problem_here: The guard blocks direct edits of frozen paths, but a training script can still reach evaluation code or held-out data indirectly; the README calls the guard a seatbelt.
mechanism: Controller-side hash check of frozen paths against the approved plan; evaluation executed in a separate process from a clean checkout of the evaluator; the reported metric is recomputed by the harness and compared with what the run printed; a diff of the workspace per iteration stored in the ledger.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.11337 (2026-03-11, authors: evaluator-tampering attempts in about 50% of natural-agent episodes, removed by evaluator locking at 25 to 31% median runtime overhead; one defence blocks one route, locking plus data-access control blocks both); https://nickoak.com/posts/tennis-xgboost-autoresearch/ (2026-03-18, practitioner: a mutable evaluator file let the loop report 0.8523 against an honest peak of 0.7609); https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.38882 (2026-10-28: grader hijack and label leakage in real trajectories); https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.07682 (13.8% of rollouts tried to exploit the verifier).
maturity: Paper v1 2026-03-11 (abstract read); the mechanism is standard practice in benchmark harnesses that use separate verifier containers.
cost: Medium: process isolation without containers is weaker on native Windows; the 25 to 31% overhead was measured in the paper's setting; real read-blocking of data needs OS permissions or a container, which is an optional module.
simpler_alternative: Current path-based guard plus settings deny rules.
reason: The base rate of tampering is too high to leave the evaluator reachable; hash-and-recompute is stdlib, with container isolation as the optional stronger tier.
cheap_local_trial: In a toy repository let a scripted change monkey-patch the metric function from the training script; confirm the recomputed score differs, the loop stops and the ledger names the changed file.

candidate: Planted-shortcut canary and cheater fixtures in the self-test (BaitBench, Findings of EMNLP 2026; cheater engine in renee-jia/scholar-loop, commit 2026-11-09)
what: A tiny bundled task where a cheat is available and scores better on the visible metric but fails a hidden check, plus scripted adversaries that attempt each known cheat, run by the self-test command.
problem_here: After an install or upgrade nobody knows whether the guards actually hold on this machine and agent product.
mechanism: CPU-only fake runs: scripted cheats (edit evaluator, read sealed path, print a fake metric, hard-code answers, substitute a checkpoint) must all be rejected; optionally a live agent is given the canary task and the harness records whether it took the bait.
evidence: https://aclanthology.org/2026.findings-emnlp.2477/ (Findings of EMNLP 2026, landing page, authors: 57.1% of runs took the planted shortcut, five of seven agents above 50%, and an explicit instruction not to cheat left the mean above 50%); https://github.com/renee-jia/scholar-loop (2026-11-09, MIT, 188 tests, self-reported: a bundled cheater proves the guards).
maturity: Benchmark paper 2026; the fixture idea is one small repository's practice (474 stars, weak signal).
cost: Low for scripted cheats; the live-agent canary costs tokens and can only show presence of cheating, not absence.
simpler_alternative: The existing 38 guard-decision tests.
reason: Turns the guard claims into something a user can check in minutes; the scripted part fits the existing test style.
cheap_local_trial: Add three scripted cheats to the existing fake-run tests and run them on native Windows and WSL2; all three must be denied or detected.

candidate: Noise-aware keep rule: measured noise floor (median absolute deviation over repeated baseline runs) and a smoke, verify, full seed funnel (pi-autoresearch v1.9.0; renee-jia/scholar-loop)
what: Before the loop starts the harness measures run-to-run spread of the incumbent; a change is kept only if its gain exceeds a multiple of that spread, confirmed on extra seeds before it becomes the incumbent.
problem_here: No kept result may depend on a lucky seed, and single-run comparisons are what an agent does by default.
mechanism: Baseline repeated 3 or more times; noise = median absolute deviation; a candidate passes smoke (short run), then verify (3 seeds), then full (5 seeds) only if earlier tiers pass; paired alternating runs when hardware load varies; the seed runs count against the budget.
evidence: https://github.com/davebcn87/pi-autoresearch (v1.9.0, 2026-10-07: gain divided by median absolute deviation, 2.0 or more called likely real; advisory only, no validation of the thresholds); https://github.com/renee-jia/scholar-loop (funnel with 3 and 5 seeds, self-reported); https://elianaive.com/posts/another-typical-autoresearch-post/ (2026-07-31, practitioner: a byte-identical submission swung 20% between runs); https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.26499 (2026-04-13, Meta: apparent overfitting in earlier agent work stems from evaluation noise).
maturity: Robust statistics are textbook; the loop-specific thresholds are unvalidated conventions from two repositories.
cost: Multiplies GPU cost per kept change by 3 to 8; with 5-minute runs that is affordable, with 5-hour runs it is not, so the tier sizes must be user-set; three baseline runs give a crude spread estimate.
simpler_alternative: A fixed minimum-improvement threshold chosen by the user.
reason: Directly required by the first quality attribute and implementable with the statistics module.
cheap_local_trial: Run the same 2-minute training five times with different seeds, compute the spread, then feed the loop a no-op change and a real improvement and check which is kept.

candidate: Delta-anomaly circuit breaker and prediction sanity checks (practitioner case, tennis prediction write-up 2026-03-18)
what: The loop demands extra confirmation when one iteration's gain is far above the recent average, and the evaluator runs output checks that catch hard-coded or degenerate predictions.
problem_here: A cheat that slips past file guards shows up first as a gain that is too good.
mechanism: Trigger when a gain exceeds a multiple of the rolling mean of kept gains; checks such as prediction variance, dependence on input, and score on a shuffled-label or held-out slice.
evidence: https://nickoak.com/posts/tennis-xgboost-autoresearch/ (2026-03-18, one practitioner: about 14 basis points per iteration when honest against about 153 during manipulation; the 3-times threshold is the author's suggestion, untested). Same failure class measured in https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.38882 and https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.21384. The threshold itself is Unverified.
maturity: A single write-up; anomaly thresholds are a common engineering practice.
cost: Low; false triggers on genuine breakthroughs would stop an unattended loop, so the action should be extra confirmation runs, not a halt.
simpler_alternative: Rely on the confirmation split and seed funnel alone.
reason: Cheap second line of defence, but the trigger value has no evidence behind it and needs tuning on real loops.
cheap_local_trial: Replay the kept-gain sequence from a toy loop with one injected 10-times gain and check that the breaker demands confirmation runs for that iteration only.

candidate: Prevent, persist, redirect: pre-run check on sampled data, automatic revert on failure, durable lessons, stagnation-triggered redirect (arXiv 2609.30541 v1; validation hooks in arXiv 2611.00384 v1)
what: Each proposed change gets a short smoke run before the full run, failures revert automatically, lessons and prohibitions live in harness-owned storage, and a redirect step fires only when the harness detects stagnation.
problem_here: Unattended loops lose a fifth to a third of iterations to crashes and repeat forbidden experiments.
mechanism: Smoke tier of a few steps on sampled data catching out-of-memory, shape and dataloader errors; revert to the incumbent commit on any failed run; refusal list enforced in code; stagnation = relative best gain under a threshold over a window, which changes the next brief (or calls the reviewer role) and clears at the next keep.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.30541 (2026-09-24, ICDM 2026 applied track, one organisation, observational: infrastructure faults in 18% and 37% of iterations; a code check before execution fixed 14 latent bugs; revert fired in 4 of 21 iterations; Recall@6 4.17% to 5.48% with the pre-run fixer and 6.90% with a critic fired under 8% gain over 5 iterations); https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00384 (2026-10-30, LinkedIn: executable validation hooks on sampled data before full-scale training; 92 of 115 generated runs completed).
maturity: Production reports from two organisations in 2026; the first released no code and its ablation is sequential and observational.
cost: Smoke runs add minutes per iteration; the paper's fixer and critic are extra agents (the brief's evidence warns against delegation), so start with the deterministic parts.
simpler_alternative: Let failed runs count as discarded iterations.
reason: Addresses the most common unattended failure with deterministic parts that fit the run controller; the agent-based parts need their own evidence.
cheap_local_trial: Inject an out-of-memory batch size and a wrong tensor shape into a toy training change and confirm the smoke tier rejects both in under a minute and the workspace returns to the incumbent.

candidate: Guard metrics: non-target floors checked on every keep (MMPostTrainBench arXiv 2610.05398 v1; Verify and Guard in uditgoenka/autoresearch v2.3.0; capability-floor gate in SoL-Pi)
what: Besides the target metric the user declares metrics that must not fall below a floor; a change that improves the target and breaks a floor is rejected.
problem_here: Loops optimise the one number they are shown and silently damage everything else, which for language-model fine-tuning means lost general capability.
mechanism: Config lists guard metrics with tolerances, measured by the frozen evaluator at baseline; the keep rule requires every guard within tolerance and the target improved beyond noise.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.05398 (2026-10-04, authors: 52.1% of model-task means fell below the base model, with regressions on non-target capabilities); https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25069 (2026-10-18: agents matching on the primary score were worse calibrated than simple baselines); https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.30541 (0 of 15 runs met three usability criteria together); https://nvlabs.github.io/SoL-Pi/ (every capability metric within a predeclared tolerance and at least one efficiency metric improved); https://fparisio.substack.com/p/an-ai-agent-cold-tuned-our-glm-52 (practitioner: a benchmark-shaped win failed on real traffic).
maturity: Present in the loop skills read (optional Guard command in uditgoenka/autoresearch v2.3.0, guard command in codex-autoresearch v0.6.0); measured need shown by three 2026 benchmarks.
cost: Low in code; each guard metric adds evaluation time per iteration and one more noisy comparison, so tolerances must come from measured noise.
simpler_alternative: Single target metric with the reviewer asked to look for regressions.
reason: Small extension of the existing metric config that answers a failure seen in every post-training benchmark read.
cheap_local_trial: Fine-tune a small language model for 5 minutes on one task with a second task as guard; feed a change that raises the target and drops the guard and confirm it is reverted.

candidate: Plan-hash approval for unattended runs (junjunjunbong/research-loop v0.4.1)
what: The user approves one loop plan up front; the approval is bound to a hash of the commands, metric source, editable scope, limits, resource class and base commit, and the controller refuses to act when any of these changes.
problem_here: Unattended mode has nobody to answer permission prompts, and the brief forbids bypassing approvals outside a container.
mechanism: The controller computes the plan hash at approval, stores it in the immutable run configuration, re-computes it before every iteration, and stops on mismatch; training commands run as argument arrays without a shell.
evidence: https://github.com/junjunjunbong/research-loop (v0.4.1 tag, Apache-2.0, 1 star, 26 commits; design read from the repository page; no effectiveness evidence and almost no adoption). Related: https://github.com/leo-lilinxiao/codex-autoresearch (immutable confirmed run configuration).
maturity: One very small repository; the idea is the same as signed job specifications in batch systems.
cost: Low in code; it authorises the controller's own actions only, so each agent product still needs an allow-list for the agent's tool calls, which differs across the three products.
simpler_alternative: A fixed allow-list of commands in each product's settings.
reason: A clean, dependency-free answer to a hard constraint, but unproven; needs a trial on all three products.
cheap_local_trial: Approve a toy plan, change the metric name in the config mid-loop, and confirm the next iteration refuses to start with a clear message.

candidate: Number grounding: every number in a journal entry or final report must resolve to a ledger record (VerifiedRegistry in renee-jia/scholar-loop; consistency patterns in wanshuiyin/Anti-Autoresearch v0.5)
what: A deterministic check that extracts numbers from the report and fails unless each one matches a value the harness itself measured, with the aggregation it claims (mean over seeds, not best seed).
problem_here: Whoever reads a reported number must know it was measured; agents overclaim and report numbers that conflict with their own records.
mechanism: Report numbers carry a run or ledger reference; a stdlib checker compares value, rounding and aggregation against the ledger and lists unbound or mismatching numbers; the reviewer role proposes findings and code decides.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19159 (2026-10-13, authors: 114 of 135 agent-written papers failed an integrity check, most often claimed work never done and numbers conflicting with recorded evidence); https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.14905 (2026-08-25: overclaiming with concealed negatives in 78.1%, report-to-code traceability gap in 60.5% of analyses); https://github.com/wanshuiyin/Anti-Autoresearch (MIT, v0.5: deterministic adjudicator, only 7 of 46 patterns tested on the author's fixtures); https://github.com/renee-jia/scholar-loop (self-reported).
maturity: Need shown by two 2026 studies; implementations are two small repositories without external validation.
cost: Low to medium; free-text reports make extraction brittle, so the report template should make references explicit; does not catch wrong interpretation of correct numbers.
simpler_alternative: Ask the reviewer subagent to cross-check numbers by reading.
reason: Protects the third user in the brief (the later reader) with a cheap deterministic check.
cheap_local_trial: Write a report with one correct number, one best-seed number labelled as a mean and one invented number against a toy ledger; the checker must flag exactly the last two.

candidate: Run-directory reviewer with blocking findings (agent-as-a-judge and uncorrected self-awareness, How Do Agents Fail on AutoResearch arXiv 2608.14905 v3)
what: The read-only reviewer inspects the run directory, diff and ledger against a short pattern list instead of the agent's summary, and each finding becomes an open item that harness code refuses to close until the code or the claim changes.
problem_here: Agents notice flaws in their own work and report the unrevised result anyway; a reviewer whose findings are advisory repeats that failure one level up.
mechanism: Reviewer output is a list of pattern id, quoted evidence span and file; the controller records open findings in the ledger; a final report or a keep is refused while a blocking finding is open or unanswered.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.14905 (2026-08-25, authors, 800 trajectories: uncorrected self-awareness in 82.5% of analyses; an agent judge at pattern level reached F1 83.0 and kappa 0.75 against F1 66.7 and kappa 0.53 for a single-prompt judge on 50 human-labelled trajectories); https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.17906 (independent evidence review: 5 audit-confirmed issues against 11 to 27 for other systems, authors); limit: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.38882 (best monitor F1 64.88 at finding hacked commands).
maturity: Evaluation paper v3 2026-08-25; the orchestration fix is not tested by its authors.

maturity: Research topic of 2026; results depend on held-out tasks and size control.
cost: Many agent runs per edit; high risk of overfitting a handful of tasks and of growing the default text, against the low-burden attribute.
simpler_alternative: Hand edits measured on held-out tasks with a size budget for the default text.
reason: Do not automate; adopt the lesson that any change to kit text is judged on tasks it was not tuned on and under a size cap.
cheap_local_trial: none

candidate: Agent-launched cloud jobs through a launcher skill (vendor write-up, scaling autoresearch on 16 rented GPUs, 2026-03-18)
what: The agent itself starts, monitors and collects training jobs on rented GPUs through a cluster launcher.
problem_here: Goal 3 (optional remote training) and the question of whether parallel remote runs speed up a loop.
mechanism: A launcher skill gives the agent commands to submit jobs to a pool of rented machines and fetch results.
evidence: https://skypilot.ai/blog/scaling-autoresearch/ (2026-03-18, vendor blog: about 910 experiments in 8 hours on 16 GPUs, about 700 valid, about 9 times faster than a simulated sequential baseline, estimated under 300 dollars of GPU and about 9 dollars of model API; the faster GPU type ran about 9% more steps in the same 5-minute budget so rankings did not transfer; no autostop, budget cap or teardown is described). Vendor self-report.
maturity: One vendor demonstration.
cost: Money, accounts and credentials on rented machines; letting the agent launch means the agent can spend; mixed GPU types break comparisons under wall-clock budgets.
simpler_alternative: The controller, not the agent, submits remote runs under a user cap, on one GPU type, with step budgets.
reason: Shows the throughput on offer and exactly which safeguards a kit module must add; the tool choice belongs to the remote-GPU facet.
cheap_local_trial: None without an account; a dry-run launcher that only prints the plan and the cost cap can be tested locally in minutes.

candidate: Install-time check for conflicting skills, hooks and instruction files (When Safe Skills Collide arXiv 2606.00448)
what: At install and upgrade the installer lists other skills, hooks and instruction files in the repository that could override or contradict the kit's rules.
problem_here: The kit is installed into repositories that already carry other agent extensions; a loop skill that tells the agent to disable permissions would undo the guard.
mechanism: Scan known extension locations of the three products for hook registrations on the same events, permission-widening settings and instruction text matching a short pattern list; report, do not modify.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.00448 (2026-05-30, authors: 651 individually safe skills, 211,575 pairs, 22.25% flagged, 18.2% validated, about 14K real compositional risks; recommends install-time composition checks and capability isolation). Three loop READMEs read in this sweep advise bypassing permissions.
maturity: One measurement paper; the installer check itself is untested.
cost: Low; pattern lists go stale and produce false alarms; cannot see user-level or enterprise settings on every product.
simpler_alternative: A paragraph in the README telling users to review other extensions.
reason: Cheap and aimed at a real interaction risk, but its usefulness depends on what the three products expose, which the platform scouts know better.
cheap_local_trial: Install the kit into a temp repository that already holds a hook on the same event and a permission-widening setting; check both are reported.

candidate: Blind variation, selective retention for the hypothesis step (arXiv 2611.12184 v1)
what: Generate ideas with deliberately limited task information to widen exploration, then use outcomes of earlier verified proposals to choose which ideas deserve a run.
problem_here: Loops drift into tuning-only iterations and near-duplicates.
mechanism: Two prompts with different information: a sparse one for proposing, a history-rich one for ranking; the ranking step may discard a share of candidates before any GPU time.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.12184 (2026-11-09, authors, 5 proposer models, 12 scientific tasks: higher originality and more high-utility proposals; selection discarded half the candidates while keeping most top performers; no numbers in the abstract). Related base rate: https://benchmarks.bespokelabs.ai/autoresearchexam/ (tuning-only rounds from 7.0% to 55.5% depending on the model).
maturity: Two days old at the time of checking, abstract only, no code link.
cost: Extra model calls per iteration; originality scores are not training outcomes.
simpler_alternative: One proposal per fresh session with duplicate refusal.
reason: Fits the fresh-session loop and costs no dependency, but the evidence is an abstract on non-training tasks.
cheap_local_trial: On the 5-minute task ask for 6 proposals with and without the past-results digest and compare how many are tuning-only or duplicates.

candidate: Evidence-preserving reducer for delegated log summaries (SoL-Pi project page, paper arXiv 2609.20519)
what: A summary produced by a delegated reader of logs is accepted only if the lines it quotes are found verbatim in the archived log.
problem_here: The run-analyst subagent reads raw logs so the main context stays clean; nothing verifies that what it reports is in the log.
mechanism: The analyst must return quoted lines with offsets; a stdlib check searches the log for each quote and rejects the summary on a miss.
evidence: https://nvlabs.github.io/SoL-Pi/ (checked 2026-11-11, authors: one of four harness changes that survived out of 152 proposed, under two mechanical gates and a held-out set no agent saw; overall 45 to 49% fewer tokens at about 94% of the baseline score on 51 tasks; no separate number for this mechanism on the page). Related: https://github.com/wanshuiyin/Anti-Autoresearch (verbatim spans required for findings).
maturity: Project page of a 2026 paper; code at https://github.com/NVlabs/SoL-Pi, licence not stated on the page.
cost: A few lines of code; quotes can be genuine and still misinterpreted.
simpler_alternative: Trust the analyst summary, as today.
reason: Tiny deterministic check that removes one unverified hop in the kit's existing design.
cheap_local_trial: Give the analyst a toy log, alter one quoted line in its answer and confirm the check rejects it.
